concepts.name: Portal Workspace: Refined Sections, completed
concepts.ia:
**Objects and scopes.**
- Organisation → Property.
- A Property has one Property look, its Portal groups (scoped to the property, at most one group per portal) and its Portals.
- A Portal has:
  - a Place: an admin-only name, a place type and a group;
  - one shared Draft (the working copy);
  - numbered Versions: immutable snapshots with append-only activations;
  - a Code: the token plus its QR and NFC artifacts, and later named placements;
  - Measures, Health, Responsible managers and Activity.

The IA encodes one rule. Anything the whole property shares is edited in exactly one place, Property look, by an Account admin. That covers composition, the three colours, the display name (linked out to Profile), the fallback wording and the trusted link destinations. Anything a single place owns is edited in its workspace by a Property manager. That covers the welcome line, the description, useful links, the note offer, languages, the place and its group, the code, and the responsible managers.

**Pages and routes.**
- `/portals`: All properties portals. New, org scope.
- `/properties/$id/portals`: Portals overview, with the list, the groups and the portfolio figures.
- `/properties/$id/portals/new`: New portal, Place step.
- `/properties/$id/portals/$portalId?tab=experience|share|analytics|activity`: the Portal workspace. It replaces today's Settings, Links, Share and Analytics tabs.
- `/properties/$id/portals/$portalId/review`: Review & publish. It has its own route so it can be linked.
- `/properties/$id/portals/look`: Property look. `/look/review` is the batch publish after a look change.
- `/properties/$id/portals/groups/$groupId`: Group analytics. It uses the same Analytics layout at group scope and lists the group's portals alphabetically.

**Where today's Settings content goes. 'Settings' stops being a concept.**
- Publication toggle → header facts, the review dock and the header overflow ('Pause public page').
- Publication history → the Activity ledger, now with restore.
- Google destination card → a health check. Its fix lives in Integrations.
- Guest languages → Experience › Languages.
- Property brand, property fallback content and approved destinations → Property look.
- Portal override → Experience › Welcome.
- Responsible managers → Activity › Responsible.
- Name → Experience › Place and group. The slug moves to header overflow › 'Portal details'.
- Description and the legacy theme presets → retired (they never reach guests).
- Threshold → Experience › Rating and Google.
- Content review attestation → Activity.
- The Links tab → Experience › Useful links.
- The 'Portal groups' section under the table → group header rows and the Place and group field.
concepts.navigation:
**Sidebar.**
- In property scope, the existing 'Portals' row (globe icon, `portal.read`) opens the Portals overview.
- In org scope the row stops being inert and opens `/portals` (All properties), the same way Reviews opens `/inbox`.
- Opening a portal workspace collapses the sidebar to the 48px icon rail (the Inbox's workspace mode B). Going back to the overview restores it.

**Wayfinding.**
- Standard pages (overview, New portal, All properties) use the PageHeader breadcrumb, e.g. 'Properties › Avela Resort › Portals'.
- The workspace and Property look use a ghost 'Portals' back link in the 56px header. It returns to the overview with its filters intact, because they live in the URL.
- Switching property from inside a workspace lands on the other property's Portals overview, never on a missing portal.

**URL holds the state**, so a manager can send a colleague the exact view:
- `?tab`, `?section=welcome`, `?preview=after-2`, `?lang=bg`, `?source=draft|live`, `?range=90d`;
- on the overview: `?show=attention`, `?group=dining`, `?sort=`.

**Landing tab.** An explicit `?tab` wins. Otherwise the workspace opens on Activity when the portal needs attention, and on Experience in every other case.

**Deep links.**
- `portal.health_attention` → `?tab=activity`, with the failing check first. Today it opens the Settings tab.
- `portal.responsibility_needed` → `?tab=activity#responsible`.
- Private notes stay in the Inbox. Its Feedback queue gains a portal facet, and each row shows the source, e.g. '· Reception portal'.
- The setup checklist step 'Publish a portal' opens the overview and gains a needs_admin state.
- Dashboard › Overview gains a 'Qualified scans' tile and an attention chip, e.g. '1 portal needs attention', that opens `?show=attention`.

**Keyboard.**
- Workspace tabs are a tablist (arrow keys).
- Sections are disclosure buttons.
- The preview is one labelled tab stop.
- Esc closes sheets and returns focus to the control that opened them.

screens.name: 1. Portals overview (property)
screens.purpose: Answer in one look: which of my places needs me, which are live, and are guests using them. It is the entry to every portal, group and the property look.
screens.layout:
Standard page (mode A), dashboard width (1136 at 1440). PageHeader: breadcrumb 'Avela Resort › Portals', h1 'Portals', actions [Property look] outline 36 plus [New portal] primary 36.

A property-wide cause line appears only when there is one. It has no box: 14px, triangle glyph plus words, e.g. 'Google link unavailable for Avela Resort · affects 4 live portals · Account admin: Elena Petrova', with the link 'Open Google connection'.

Summary strip: a hairline-split dl on #feffff with four cells:
- 'Needs attention 1' (filter button);
- 'Live 3 of 5';
- 'Changes not live 2' (filter button);
- 'Private notes waiting 2' (link to Inbox Feedback for this property's portals).

Toolbar: search (288) · 'Show: All ⌄' · 'Group by: Group ⌄' · spacer · range select '90 days ⌄' (the shared ?range=).

Table, in the property-list pattern (white, radius 8), with these columns:
- Portal, 300: name link 14/500, meta 12px 'Reception desk · QR and NFC · EN, БГ'.
- Status, 224: fact '● Live · v5'. A second line appears only when needed: '2 changes not live' in neutral ink, or 'Partly working · no one responsible' in #a45f00 with a glyph.
- Qualified scans, 96.
- Private ratings, 96.
- Average, 96: '4.4' plus a gold star 14. Below 5 ratings it reads 'Too few' in #5b5d63.
- Opened Google, 96.
- Private notes, 96.
- Responsible, 80: 20px owner discs.
- Actions, 56: ellipsis.

Group header rows are 44px on #f7f8fa, 13px 500, e.g. 'Dining · 2 portals · 1 needs attention', with summed figures in the same columns. Ungrouped portals sit under 'Not in a group'. A final 'All portals' row (500 weight, border-top #b5b7bd) carries the property totals: this is the portfolio figure. Draft rows merge the five metric cells into one sentence, 'Not published yet'. Under the table, one muted line: 'Last 90 days · Average needs 5 private ratings · Sorted by what needs attention, then name.'
screens.keyInteractions:
The portal name is the row's one link. It opens the workspace on Activity when the portal needs attention, otherwise on Experience.

Strip cells filter the table and write ?show=. Column headers sort, but there are no rank numbers, medals or best/worst tints. The default sort is 'needs attention, then name', and 'Clear' restores it.

Menus:
- Group header ⋯: Rename · Group analytics · Archive group (Account admin).
- Row ⋯: Open · Try as guest · Download print kit · Move to group… · Pause public page… · Archive…
- The Archived filter offers Restore. A restored portal comes back as Paused.

A property with no portals shows the dashed EmptyState 'No portals yet' with 'A portal is the page guests reach from a code at a place such as reception or a table.' and [New portal].

If the property look is incomplete (fields only an Account admin can set), a Property manager sees one sentence above the table: 'An Account admin needs to finish the property look before any portal can go live. You can still prepare drafts.' with [Ask an Account admin].

screens.name: 2. All properties · Portals (org scope)
screens.purpose: Give an Account admin, or a Property manager with several properties, one exception-first view across properties without comparing them.
screens.keyInteractions:
- The property header link opens that property's overview. Expand and collapse is remembered per viewer.
- The 'New guest wording available' cell opens a batch review. It lists every portal's wording diff and checks, with a checkbox to leave any out, and one primary action, 'Publish 11 portals'.
- Property managers see only the properties assigned to them (D6-001 reads).
- Search spans portal and property names.
- The default order is attention, then property name. There is no cross-property ranking and no 'top property' framing.

screens.name: 3. New portal · Place
screens.purpose: Step 1 of creation. Start from where guests meet the portal, not from a name, slug and theme.

screens.name: 4. Portal workspace · Experience
screens.purpose: The everyday editor. Change what this place says and shows, and see the exact guest page while doing it.
screens.layout:
Workspace (mode B): 48px icon rail and 52px top bar.

Header (56, border-b, padding 0 24), left to right:
- a ghost 'Portals' back link;
- the title 'Reception' 14/600 over 'Avela Resort' 12px;
- a fact group: '● Live · version 5' (a detail: 'Published 12 Sep by Elena Petrova · codes open this version') and '3 changes not live' with a pencil glyph (a detail whose popover lists them in guest words, with a 'Review changes' link);
- a health fact, only when something is wrong;
- a ghost ⋯: Rename · Duplicate · Pause public page… · Archive… · Portal details (ID, slug).

Row 2 (48) is split at the column hairline:
- Left: line tabs 'Experience · Share · Analytics · Activity'. Activity reads '· 1 issue' in #a45f00 when the portal needs attention.
- Right, over the stage: [Draft | Live v5] compact tabs · [Arrival ⌄] sm select · [EN | БГ] compact tabs · [Try as guest] outline sm with the smartphone icon.

Body: an editor column of 640 that scrolls, a 1px hairline, and a preview stage (flex, #f0f2f5). The stage centres a 390-wide device outline (1px #b5b7bd, radius 32, no chrome). The guest page scrolls inside the outline.

The editor has two groups, with 12px 500 #5b5d63 labels:
- 'On the guest page': Look (Property-wide) · Welcome (This portal) · Rating and Google (Always included) · Useful links (This portal).
- 'Behind the page': Languages · Place and group.

Each section row is 56px and flat, with hairlines between rows. It holds a 16px icon, a 14/500 title, a 13px secondary summary (e.g. 'Welcome to Avela · Bulgarian uses property wording'), a scope fact and a chevron. The open section's header fills #e7e4ff and its fields sit directly beneath, with no box.

The dock sits at the bottom of the column (56, border-top). Left: a save fact, 'Draft saved · 1 min ago', 'Saving…' or 'Couldn't save · Retry'. Right: the primary sm [Review & publish]. When nothing is pending, the button is replaced by the fact 'Everything is live'.
screens.keyInteractions:
**Preview binding.** Opening a section scrolls the preview to its region and outlines it: 2px #7b65d1 at a 4px offset, plus a small tag with the section name. Clicking a preview region in edit mode opens its section. The preview refreshes 300ms after typing stops. EN/БГ drives both the fields and the preview. Draft/Live switches the stage to the live snapshot, which is what guests see now. An admin-only line above the device lists anything hidden from guests, e.g. 'Hidden from guests: Spa menu · waiting for approval'.

**Welcome.** Each language has a welcome line (up to 120 characters) and a short description (up to 500). Each field is either:
- 'Using property wording': read-only text plus [Write for this portal]; or
- an override, with a 'Use property wording' reset.
When English is custom and Bulgarian is not, a fact says so: 'English is custom; Bulgarian uses property wording' with [Write Bulgarian].

**Rating and Google.**
- The pinned guest wording is shown read-only ('Guest wording v2').
- The one control is 'Offer a private note at [3★ ⌄] or below', with the helper 'Google stays the same for every guest'.
- A detail answers 'Why can't Google be hidden for low ratings?'.

**Useful links.**
- Each row holds a grip, an icon from the curated set, the label in EN or BG, and an approval fact shown only when the link is not approved: 'Waiting for an Account admin · hidden from guests' or 'Failed its check · hidden'.
- Row ⋯: Edit · Move up · Move down · Remove. Remove is a draft operation, with Undo in the toast.
- [Add link] is an outline button. After four rows, a fact reads 'Guests see up to 4 links'.
- Tripadvisor and Booking addresses are labelled 'Find us on …' automatically.

**Place and group.** Name, place type, group, and 'Evening placement: night edition' (Folio only).

**Look.** Facts only: composition, colour swatches with names, display name. An Account admin sees [Edit property look]. A Property manager sees 'Set by an Account admin · Elena Petrova'.

screens.name: 5. Preview states and the fairness view
screens.purpose: Let the manager check every state a guest can reach, and prove that the Google action is identical for every score.
screens.layout:
The stage's state select opens a grouped menu:
- Before rating: Arrival · Rating chosen · Couldn't send.
- After rating: 2★ Fair · 5★ Excellent · Writing a private note · Done.
- Not available: Google can't be opened · Page not available (paused, archived or code turned off; brand-free and identical for every reason, per the round-3 rules).
- Separated from the groups: 'Compare 1★ and 5★'.

The compare view fills the same stage with two device outlines at 0.9 scale (351 wide, 24 gap), captioned '1★ Poor' and '5★ Excellent'. The Google card sits at the same height in both. On the 1★ side an admin marker (a 1px dashed #edcb85 bracket and 12px #a45f00 text) labels the private-note card 'Added at 3★ or below · your setting'. The figcaption reads 'Same Google action for every rating.'
screens.keyInteractions:
- States use fixture guest input and never call guest actions.
- A state the current settings cannot produce is labelled in the menu, e.g. 'Private note: offered at 3★ or below'.
- The Rating and Google section links straight to the compare view.
- Below 1280 the compare view opens as a full-width overlay with 'Close comparison'.
- ?preview= makes any state shareable with a colleague.

screens.name: 6. Try as guest
screens.purpose: Walk the whole flow the way a guest would, including the failure states, with a guarantee that nothing is recorded.
screens.keyInteractions:
- Stars, send, the note composer, the 'Your response' disclosure and the language links all work.
- 'Continue to Google' swaps the frame to an in-frame card, 'Google would open here', with Back.
- The simulated failure shows the real error copy and Try again.
- Esc closes the sheet and returns focus to the button.
- The sheet is backed by a preview-only resolver. It holds no portal token and cannot reach public guest endpoints.

screens.name: 7. Review & publish
screens.purpose: One decision point. It shows what guests will see change, every blocker with the person who can fix it, and what else is waiting.
screens.layout:
Its own route. The workspace header stays. Row 2 left becomes '← Back to editing · Review changes to Reception'. The stage gets [Live v5 | After publishing] and shows 'After publishing' by default.

The review column (640) has three blocks with 16/500 headings:

1. **'What guests will see change'.** One row per change, in guest words, with its language, e.g.:
   - 'Welcome line · English: "Reception" → "Welcome to Avela"';
   - 'Useful links: added "Spa menu", which stays hidden until spa.avela.bg is approved';
   - 'Look (property-wide): accent colour changed by Elena Petrova · 17 Sep'.
2. **'Checks'.** Only failures and warnings are listed. The six checks that passed (public code, responsible manager, Google link, look complete, wording for every language, colour contrast) fold into the detail '6 checks passed'. Each row has a glyph, a sentence, 'Who can fix' and one control. Examples:
   - a warning: 'Bulgarian guests will still read the property wording "Добре дошли в Avela Resort".' with [Write Bulgarian];
   - a blocker only an Account admin can fix: 'Bulgarian property wording is missing · Account admin' with [Ask an Account admin].
3. **'Also waiting on other portals'.** Shown only for property-wide changes, e.g. 'This look change is also not live on Spa & thermal pools and Pool bar.'

Dock: on the left, the fact 'Publishes as version 6'. On the right, [Back to editing] outline and one primary whose label is always the next step: 'Publish changes', 'Publish portal' (first time), 'Assign a manager', or 'Ask an Account admin'.
screens.keyInteractions:
- Clicking a change row moves the stage to that state and region and flips between Live and After.
- Blockers the current user can fix are fixed inline (the manager popover, or a jump to the field).
- Publish is one atomic swap (new command). Toast: 'Version 6 is live. Printed codes keep working.' The ledger gets an entry.
- A server refusal keeps the review open and translates the reason, e.g. 'The Google link stopped working a moment ago. Try again when it is back.'

screens.name: 8. Published · distribute (first publish)
screens.purpose: Step 4 of creation. Turn a first publish straight into something printable while the one-time address is still on screen.

screens.name: 9. Share (ongoing)
screens.purpose: Manage the code over time: where it is placed, reprints, replacement and turning it off, with printed codes surviving every edit.
screens.layout:
A 640 column plus a print-preview stage.

- **'Public code'**: facts 'Active since 3 Sep · QR and NFC · opens version 5'. [Download print kit] primary, [Copy link] outline, and ⋯ with 'Replace code…' and 'Turn off all codes…'.
- **'Where it's placed'** (new: named placements): a small table with Place · Channel · Added, e.g. 'Front desk card · QR · 3 Sep' and 'Checkout tag · NFC · 3 Sep', plus [Add placement]. The name field's helper reads 'Name a place, not a person.'
- **'Print kit'**: as in screen 8.
- **'History'**: the Timeline filtered to code events.
- A legacy notice, only when it applies: 'This code was created before scans were counted. Replace it at your next reprint so its scans count.'
screens.keyInteractions:
**Replace code** opens a dialog with two options:
- 'Planned: the old code keeps working for [30] days';
- 'Now: for a lost or misused code'.
It shows a consequence sentence and a preview of the brand-free 'not available' guest page. The ledger then reads 'Code version 1 keeps working until 18 Oct'.

**Turn off all codes** requires a reason (1–500 characters) and says how many placements go dark.

**Re-downloading without rotating** waits on the security decision. Until then the kit button becomes 'Replace code to reprint', with a detail that explains why.

screens.name: 10. Analytics (portal)
screens.purpose: An honest answer to 'is this place working for us?' in guest order, with comparisons only where the sample supports them.
screens.keyInteractions:
- When either period has fewer than 10 ratings, the average shows its n, plus one sentence, 'Too few private ratings to compare with the 90 days before.', and [Show 6 months].
- All time shows no deltas.
- The private-notes figure links to Inbox Feedback filtered to this portal (a new facet).
- Hovering a version tick shows 'Version 5 published 12 Sep by Elena Petrova'. There is no causal claim.
- Never shown: Google opens by star, staff, or this portal against other portals.

screens.name: 11. Activity (health, responsibility, ledger)
screens.purpose: Monitoring and history for one portal: what is wrong and who fixes it, who is responsible, and everything that happened, with restore.

screens.name: 12. Property look (Account admin)
screens.purpose: Brand governance. It holds one composition, three colours with derived roles, the fallback wording and the trusted destinations for the whole property, shows which portals a change affects, and never silently changes a live page.
screens.layout:
Workspace geometry (editor 640 | stage). Header: 'Property look' with 'Avela Resort', and the fact 'Used by 5 portals · 3 live' (a detail that lists them). Row 2 right: 'Preview on: Reception ⌄' · state · EN/БГ.

Sections:
- **Composition**: three choice cards with 64px thumbnails (Carved Stillness · Folio · Table Card) and the fact 'Suggested for your colours: Folio'. A composition that cannot carry the brand says why, e.g. 'Stars would be too faint on the dark stage with this accent', and cannot be selected.
- **Colours**: Text, Background and Accent hex inputs with 20px swatches. Derived roles are listed as facts: 'Stars and rules · #7A5C3E · passes' and 'Button label · white'. A failure reads 'Accent too light for stars on paper' with [Use #6E5234]. Raw ratios are never shown.
- **Name on guest pages**: the fact 'Avela Resort' plus a link to Property settings › Profile, noting 'also used in AI replies'.
- **Property wording**: EN and БГ title and short description, required for every language offered.
- **Trusted link destinations**: rows of host · state · requested by. Pending rows have [Approve] and [Decline…].

Dock: on the left, the impact detail 'Saving changes the draft of 5 portals. Live pages stay as they are until published.' On the right, [Save look] primary. After a save the dock becomes '3 live portals are waiting to publish this look' with [Review & publish 3 portals].
screens.keyInteractions:
- 'Preview on' switches the stage among portals, each with its own welcome line under the new look.
- The batch review lists each portal with its own guest-worded changes and checks, with checkboxes to leave some out, and one primary action, 'Publish 3 portals'.
- Every save and publish is written to each affected portal's ledger, and portals with an open workspace get a toast.
- A Property manager sees all of it as facts ('Set by an Account admin · Elena Petrova') with no disabled buttons. A Property manager requests destinations from a link row, not from here.

screens.name: 13. Phone: triage, quick edit, reprint (390)
screens.purpose: The jobs a manager does from a phone: act on an alert, fix a word, publish, and send the kit to the printer.
screens.layout:
16px gutters. Controls are 44 on the overview and 36 in the workspace (inbox density).

**Overview.**
- The summary strip is 2×2.
- Portals are two-line list rows: name plus status fact, then '412 scans · 4.4 from 118 · 64 opened Google'.
- Group headers become 13px labels.
- One 'Show' select replaces the filters.

**Workspace.**
- The header (56) holds the back arrow, the name and one fact (health if any, otherwise Live or Draft).
- The tabs become a scrollable line-tab row.
- Experience: sections at full width and a sticky dock with [Preview] outline and [Review & publish] primary. Preview opens a full-height sheet with the guest page at native width and no device frame, because the phone is the device. Its top bar holds Draft/Live · state · EN/БГ · Close.
- Share: [Download print kit] and [Share…].
screens.keyInteractions:
- A health notification opens ?tab=activity with the failing check and its fix at the top.
- Wording edits autosave.
- Review & publish is a full-screen step.
- The property look can be read on a phone, but editing it is desktop-first (the layout stacks and has no stage split).

concepts.createFlow:
There are four steps, each a real screen, and none asks for an admin concept a guest never sees.

**1. Place** (`/portals/new`).
- Pick where guests meet the portal, from 6 place types.
- Confirm the prefilled internal name.
- Optionally pick a group.
- Start from property wording or from a copy of another portal.
- 'Create draft' calls createPortal (name, hidden derived slug, threshold 3) plus the new place fields. The creator becomes responsible if eligible.
- Slug, description and theme are never asked.

**2. Experience** (the workspace, with Welcome open).
- The place type offers a one-click suggestion, e.g. 'Use "Welcome to the Spa" / "Добре дошли в спа центъра"'. It is never applied silently.
- Links are optional.
- The preview is live from the first keystroke. Everything autosaves.
- The dock reads 'Draft saved · Not published' with [Review & publish].

**3. Review.**
- For a first publish, 'What guests will see' lists the welcome line per language, the links, the pinned rating wording and the look.
- Checks list only what fails, each with its owner. Typical first-portal blockers:
  - the property look or fallback wording is missing (Account admin). 'Ask an Account admin' sends an in-app request that names the missing item;
  - the Google link is not verified (Account admin, in Integrations);
  - no responsible manager (anyone with `portal.update`, fixed in an inline popover);
  - the public code, which is created automatically at publish.
- The primary button's label is always the next step.

**4. Publish & distribute.**
- 'Publish portal' issues the code and publishes version 1 in one action (the existing issue and publish, in sequence).
- It lands on Share with the code on screen and the print kit preselected from the place type.
- The toast carries the guarantee: 'Reception is live. Codes open version 1.'
- The setup checklist step completes.

**Afterwards.**
- An abandoned draft shows as 'Draft · not published' in the overview, and 'Continue' resumes at Experience.
- A Property manager at a property whose look is incomplete can still finish steps 1 to 3. Step 3 names the Account admin and offers the request. The setup step shows needs_admin instead of 'pending', so nobody is told to do something they cannot finish.
concepts.editorModel:
Refined Sections, made flat and tied to a truthful preview.

**Structure.**
- Six sections in two labelled groups:
  - on the guest page, in guest order: Look, Welcome, Rating and Google, Useful links;
  - behind the page: Languages, Place and group.
- One section is open at a time, and its fields open in place under a #e7e4ff header. No section has a box.
- Each row states its scope as a fact: 'This portal', 'Property-wide' or 'Always included'.

**Saving.**
- One shared draft per portal, autosaved per field after 800ms.
- Three save states in the dock: 'Saving…', 'Draft saved · 1 min ago', and 'Couldn't save · Retry'. A failed save keeps the local text and stops publishing until the save succeeds.
- Removing a link or turning off a language is a draft operation with Undo in the toast. There are no red buttons beside ordinary edits.

**Inheritance.** Each localized field is either 'Using property wording' (read-only text plus [Write for this portal]) or an override with a 'Use property wording' reset, which sets the override to null. When languages differ, the editor says so: 'English is custom; Bulgarian uses property wording'.

**Languages.** One EN/БГ switch drives both the fields and the preview. Native language names are used, never flags. Enabling a language never implies its wording is approved.

**Links.**
- Labels in EN and BG; icons from a curated iconKey set.
- Approval state is shown in place, and only when a link is not live-eligible. Today unapproved links are dropped silently.
- Drag plus Move up and Move down (WCAG 2.5.7).
- A soft cap of 4 visible links.
- 'Group under headings' is off by default. Folio uses the headings in its index.
- A Property manager can request a destination from the link row. Approval stays with the Account admin.

**Not editable, shown as read-only facts.** The question, buttons and receipts from language pack v2, and the display name.

**Preview.**
- The public renderer runs in an iframe, fed by a new 'working copy as guest DTO' read, or by the 'snapshot as guest DTO' read for Live and for older versions.
- It follows the same resolution rules as the guest page: localized title fallback, brand profile, composition fonts, approved-link filtering, and the degraded Google state.
- In edit mode it is inert: one tab stop, labelled 'Guest preview: Reception, draft, arrival, English'. It becomes interactive only in Try as guest.
- Section and region are bound both ways, as a pointer shortcut. The keyboard path is the section list.

**Concurrency.** Field-level last-write-wins. The dock names another editor who saved within 5 minutes ('Georgi edited 2 min ago'). A property look change arrives as a toast plus a pending change.

**Accessibility.** Targets are 32px on desktop and 36px on phone. Focus is never hidden under the dock (scroll-padding-bottom 72). Every icon-only button has a name.
concepts.publishModel:
**States**, shown as facts, never as a toggle:
- Draft (never published);
- Live · version N;
- Paused (today's 'disabled');
- Archived.

The header always shows the live version and the number of changes that are not live yet. Today's 'Publish portal / Disable public page' toggle is removed.

**Publish changes.** A new snapshot plus an atomic activation swap while the portal is live. This is a new command, because published to published is a no-op today and forces disable-then-republish with an outage. Versions are numbered and only go up.
- Publishing always goes through the review step. The only multi-portal publish is the batch review after a property-wide change or a new guest wording pack.
- A language change and a publish are sequenced out of sight: the languages are saved first, then the portal is published.
- The existing content-review attestation stays separate, in Activity.

**Restore (rollback).**
- Uses the existing `rollbackPortalPublication`: only while live, and only to a lower version.
- It appends version N+1 as a copy and never rewrites history.
- It re-runs the checks on the target first, so lapsed link approvals or a broken Google link are shown before confirming.
- It leaves the draft alone, with the fact 'Your draft is based on version 6; live is version 7 (a copy of version 4)'.
- It offers Undo, which is another append.

**Pause, archive, restore.**
- 'Pause public page' sits in the header overflow. Its dialog shows the brand-free 'not available' page guests will get. The pause goes in the ledger, and codes stay valid.
- Archive makes the configuration read-only and keeps the codes.
- Restoring from the archive returns the portal as Paused. A separate publish is needed.

**Property-wide changes.**
- A look or fallback-wording save becomes a pending change on every affected draft ('Look changed · not live') and never mutates a live snapshot.
- The look page then offers a batch review that lists each portal's own diff and checks.
- A new guest wording pack works the same way: 'New guest wording' is pending on each live portal, and the review shows the EN and BG string diffs.

**Deferred.** Scheduled publishing. If it is added later, it schedules a reviewed snapshot and re-runs the checks when it fires.
concepts.distribution:
**The code outlives the content.** A token resolves to the current live version, so publishing, restoring, pausing and archiving never break print. The UI says so in two places:
- the Share fact 'Codes open the live version (5)';
- the toast 'Printed codes keep working'.

**Share tab.**
1. 'Public code': facts plus [Download print kit] (the primary), [Copy link], and overflow items 'Replace code…' and 'Turn off all codes…'.
2. 'Where it's placed': named placements.
3. 'Print kit'.
4. 'History'.

**Placements.** V1 names the existing QR and NFC artifacts ('Front desk card', 'Checkout tag'). Several named artifacts per portal (table 12, room card) are a model change that needs a decision. It is also what makes a later QR-versus-NFC and per-placement split possible. Placement names are admin-only and never guest-facing, and the helper says 'Name a place, not a person'. There is no staff dimension anywhere.

**Print kit.** It is generated per composition, so the paper matches the screen. Table Card is literally the table tent.
- Pieces: Reception card A6, Table tent A6, NFC card 85×54, Sticker 60 mm. The place type preselects one.
- Language: EN, BG or both.
- Call to action: one of two approved honest lines, never 'Review us on Google 5★'.
- Built-in rules:
  - vector PDF with 3 mm bleed and crop marks;
  - QR on a light plate with a 4-module quiet zone (today's generator uses a 2-module margin);
  - error correction M, or Q when a centre mark is ever added;
  - the short URL printed as text;
  - NFC copy that matches iOS and Android 17 ('Hold the top of your phone to the card, then tap the link');
  - a last page of NFC writing instructions: NTAG213/215/216, one NDEF URI record, lock after writing, on-metal tags near metal.
- A 'Before you print' checklist: test on two phones in low light, matte finish, no curved surfaces.
- Downloads also include SVG and PNG of the bare code.

**Re-download.** Recommended option: store the token envelope-encrypted, retrievable only by Account admins and the portal's responsible managers, with every download written to the ledger. Printers lose files, and reprinting must not mean rotating. This is a security decision. Until it is made, the kit is offered while the address is on screen after issue or publish, and later 'Replace code to reprint' explains the trade-off.

**Replace and turn off.**
- Planned replacement: grace 1–90 days, default 30. The ledger shows 'Code version 1 keeps working until 18 Oct'.
- Immediate replacement is for lost or misused codes.
- 'Turn off all codes' needs a reason.
- Each dialog shows the consequence sentence and the brand-free page guests with an old code will see.

**Legacy codes.** A pre-artifact code gets one notice only: 'Replace it at your next reprint so its scans count'.

**Test scans.** A staff member scanning the real code today counts as a qualified scan. Recommendation: exclude authenticated admin sessions on the server (a decision). Until then, the checklist says 'Your test scan counts once.'
concepts.analytics:
**Frozen vocabulary.** Each label has a dotted-underline definition.
- Qualified scans (`qualified_scans`): server-verified QR or NFC arrivals, deduplicated.
- Private ratings (`portal_rating_count`).
- Average private rating (`portal_rating_average`), always shown with its n.
- Guests who opened Google: Google selections only, filtered by `portal_destination_kind`.
- Private notes (volume), shown with a lock glyph and the word 'private'.
- Useful links opened: a secondary figure.

Never used: 'Reviews', 'Review clicks', 'Conversions', 'CTR'. Today's bounded-window 'Scans' actually counts operational `portal.scan` while All time counts qualified scans. Every admin figure moves to qualified scans, which needs a bounded-window qualified read.

**Portal scope (the Analytics tab).**
- A five-cell strip in guest order.
- A 'From scan to Google' funnel with real counts and % of scans, never clamped. Private notes appear beside it, not as a step.
- Weekly scans with the average-rating line, and version ticks so owners can line up changes with outcomes. No causal claims.
- Rating mix.
- The useful-links figure.
- Private notes link to Inbox Feedback filtered to the portal.

**Ranges.** The app-wide `?range=` model: 30 days · 90 days · 6 months · All time, default 90 days. This replaces the tab's own 7/60-day presets, its All-time default and its localStorage. The range is the same across the dashboard, the overview and the workspace.

**Comparison.**
- Deltas are shown only for bounded ranges, against the equal prior window.
- The average compares only when both periods have at least 10 ratings. Below that there is one sentence, one action, and n beside the value.
- Deltas use a sign and an arrow in text-grade positive or negative colour. A metric that is not ready gets the availability line. Provenance ('Data through', response integrity, reconciliation) sits in details, never above the numbers.

**Portfolio.**
- The Portals overview table is the property portfolio: per-portal columns, group rollup rows and an 'All portals' total.
- Group analytics reuses the Analytics layout at group scope.
- `/portals` rolls up by property.
- Rollups count issues ('1 of 4 needs attention') and never blend a status.
- Averages are rebuilt from counts, with n.
- These scopes need new reads. Scans, notes and Google opens can sum across portal-scope reads. The property and group average needs either a widened registry scope for `portal.rating` (a governance decision) or a wrapped `queryGoalMetric` (monthly only).

**Guardrails.**
- No rank numbers, medals or 'top/bottom' labels. The default sort is attention, then name.
- Google opens are never split by star.
- No staff, shift or server dimension. The staff-participation data is never read.
- No uptime or 'live' vanity counters.

**Later:**
- QR versus NFC split (needs a retention decision);
- per-link selections;
- a weekly digest to responsible managers with the same five measures and n;
- CSV export.
concepts.monitoring:
**Health in plain words.** The domain values `healthy`, `degraded` and `unavailable` become 'Working', 'Partly working' and 'Not reachable'. Each reason gets a sentence, an owner and one fix:
- `responsibility_needed`: 'No one is responsible for this portal'. Fixed by anyone with `portal.update`: Assign a manager.
- `google_destination_awaiting_refresh`: 'Google link is refreshing. Guests can rate; the Google action says it can't be opened from here'. Nothing to do. Account admin: Open Google connection.
- `google_destination_unavailable`: 'Guests can't open Google from this portal'. Account admin: Reconnect Google.
- `public_address_unavailable`: 'No active code'. Property manager: Create code.
- `property_unavailable`: 'Avela Resort is paused'. Account admin.
- `publication_snapshot_unavailable`: 'The live version couldn't be loaded'. Publish again, or contact support.

Draft, Paused and Archived are publication states, not incidents. They never count as 'needs attention'.

**Where health shows, by exception.**
- The overview's Status column stays quiet when a portal is healthy.
- It gets a second line in #a45f00 with a glyph and words when not.
- A 'Needs attention' strip cell filters the list.
- Group and property rows count issues.
- Property-wide causes, such as the Google link, are shown once above the table with the number of portals affected, instead of being repeated on every row.
- Dashboard › Overview gains one attention chip.
- The workspace header gets a health fact, and the Activity tab gets '· 1 issue'.
- The Activity tab lists every failing check, not just the domain's single top reason, by reusing the review checks.

**History.** Health transitions become ledger events ('Google link became unavailable · 14 Sep 09:12'; 'Working again · 11:40'), folded when routine. RepKey does not probe portals, so there is no uptime percentage.

**Ownership and notifications.**
- Responsible managers are the route. The Activity tab shows them, and 'Change' edits them.
- `portal.health_attention` gets a template that names the reason and the fix and deep-links to Activity.
- `portal.responsibility_needed` goes to Account admins.
- Private notes arrive through `feedback.created` in the Inbox, which gains a portal facet.
- Each person tunes their own notifications in the existing Settings › Notifications categories. `urgent_operational` stays unmutable in-app. There is no second alert threshold competing with the Private Feedback Threshold.
- A new 'Ask an Account admin' request, in the `workflow_collaboration` category, covers blockers only an Account admin can fix.

**To verify before trusting 'Working'.** There is no health reconciliation on token revoke or when a grace period expires. A proposed advisory check would cover approved destinations that lapse and are silently hidden.

**Later.** A careful silent-failure hint, 'No scans in 14 days at a portal that usually has some; check the card', that never becomes a target or a comparison.
concepts.brandGovernance:
**One place for the property's look.** `/portals/look`, editable by Account admins only (`portal.admin`, surfaced through `canManagePropertyBrand`). It holds:
- composition: Carved Stillness, Folio, or Table Card once wordmark auto-fit and the iconKey set ship;
- three hex values: text, background, accent;
- the fallback wording per language;
- the trusted link destinations;
- the display name, as a fact linked to Profile, because it is also the AI-reply business name.

**Derived colour roles instead of pickers.** The three hex values drive an engine that produces:
- stage polarity;
- the accent, shifted in OKLab lightness to 3:1 for stars and rules and to 4.5:1 for small text;
- the idle star at a 55% mix;
- a black-or-white button label.

The admin sees 'passes' or a suggested fix with a one-click [Use #…], never a raw ratio. The same contrast rule becomes a publish check. Today only text on background is enforced.

**Suggested composition.**
- Carved Stillness when the derived accent reaches 3:1 on the dark stage.
- Otherwise Folio.
- Table Card by choice, for restaurants and loud brands.

A composition that cannot carry the brand says why and cannot be selected. The default palette changes from SaaS blue to the neutral hospitality default #1E1C1A / #F6F2EA / #7A5C3E, which lands on Folio.

**Portal-level appearance stays tiny.** Only 'Evening placement: night edition', available with Folio. Legacy per-portal theme presets and the list swatch are retired, because they never reach guests on v2 snapshots.

**Showing what a change affects, and never silently.**
- The look page carries 'Used by 5 portals · 3 live', a detail that lists them.
- Its dock says, before saving, 'Saving changes the draft of 5 portals. Live pages stay as they are until published.'
- After saving, the dock offers 'Review & publish 3 portals': a batch review with each portal's diff and checks and checkboxes to leave some out. Batch publish is a new orchestration and a decision.
- Every affected portal gets a ledger line and a pending change, plus a toast if its workspace is open.
- 'Preview on: [portal]' shows the new look under each portal's own welcome line.

**Property managers** see the look as facts ('Set by an Account admin · Elena Petrova') with no disabled buttons. They can request a destination from a link row, and they can ask an Account admin to finish blockers.

**Open decision.** A per-portal composition override, for example a hotel's Olive Terrace restaurant wanting Table Card while the resort uses Carved Stillness. The beta says no: one property, one look. A restaurant with its own brand is its own property.
concepts.mobile:
At 390, the phone jobs come first: act on an alert, fix a word, publish, and get the kit to the printer. Building a property look happens on a desktop.

**Overview.**
- 16px gutters and 44px controls, like the dashboard and Properties.
- The summary strip becomes 2×2.
- The table becomes two-line list rows: name plus status fact, then '412 scans · 4.4 from 118 · 64 opened Google'.
- Group headers become 13px labels.
- One 'Show' select replaces the filters.

**Workspace**, at inbox density (36px controls):
- A 56px header with the back arrow, the name and one fact: health if any, otherwise Live or Draft.
- Tabs become a scrollable line-tab row.
- Experience: sections at full width and a sticky dock with [Preview] outline and [Review & publish] primary.
- Preview opens a full-height sheet with the guest page at native width and no device frame, because the phone is the device. Its top bar holds Draft/Live · state · EN/БГ · Close.
- Try as guest uses the same sheet with a simulation bar.
- Review & publish is a full-screen step with the dock at the bottom.
- Share: [Download print kit] plus [Share…] through the Web Share API, so the PDF goes straight to a printer or email.
- Analytics: the strip becomes 2×2, charts shrink to the compact 160 height, and range becomes a 44px select.
- Activity: the ledger reads naturally at this width, and a notification deep link puts the failing check and its fix at the top.

**Property look** can be read on a phone, and its sections stack. Its preview uses the sheet rather than a split.

**Verification** follows the inbox's rules: stories at 320, 390 and 1440, a geometry gate that keeps the dock from ever covering the focused field, axe checks, and accessible names pinned by e2e tests.
concepts.inboxConsistency:
How each inbox principle lands:

**1. Facts, controls and details wear different clothes.**
- Facts: Live/version, 'changes not live', health, save state and scope labels are plain 13px text with a glyph and no box.
- Controls: publish, restore, download and change are outlined 32px buttons, or the one primary.
- Details: metric definitions, provenance, 'nothing is recorded' and 'used by 5 portals' carry a dotted underline and open popovers.
- The filled purple 'Published' badge and the list swatch are retired.

**2. Purple means interactive only.** Status uses a neutral dot plus words. Chart marks are neutral ink. Deltas use a sign and an arrow. The only purple on the stage is the admin selection outline and tag.

**3. Private is words, a dashed edge and amber.** Private notes carry a lock glyph and the word. The fairness view marks the note card with a dashed amber bracket. Amber is never a bare signal: warnings always come with words.

**4. Ledger timeline.** One Timeline per portal covers publishing and restores, code events, health transitions, responsibility changes and property-look fan-out. Sentences read actor · verb · object · time, and routine runs fold.

**5. One primary action per area.**
- Overview: New portal.
- Editor dock: Review & publish.
- Review: the next step (Publish changes).
- Share: Download print kit.
- Activity: the first fix.
- Property look: Save look, then Review & publish N portals.
- Analytics: none.

Guarantees live in toasts and tooltips, not standing lines: 'Printed codes keep working', 'nothing is recorded', 'Google stays the same for every guest'.

**6. Availability by exception.** Healthy portals are quiet. Thin data gets n, one sentence and one action, never a dash or a fake zero. Hidden links are named only when something is hidden.

**7. Header modes.** Search lives in the header, filters are URL state, and empty states name what is empty ('No portals yet', 'No portals match "spa"').

**8. Geometry and shell.** The workspace reuses the Inbox's mode B: 48px rail, 56px header, 48px row-2 toolbar, hairline columns and a dock at the foot of the working column. Standard pages reuse PageHeader, the summary strip and the property-list table.

**9. Measured, not guessed.** Stories, the geometry gate, axe and accessible names pinned by e2e tests. The admin stays neutral and purple, and only the guest page inside the device outline carries the property brand.
newCapabilities: Publish changes while live: a new command that builds a snapshot and swaps the activation atomically, because today published → published is a no-op (capability map C1).
Portal health read, current plus history, batched per property, using the existing getCurrent/listHistory (B1). Also check reconciliation on token revoke and when a grace period expires (C7).
Portal list projection: health, live version, pending-change count, group, managers, code status and range measures in one batched read (B2). The same shape backs /portals (A5).
Publication history with the actor (activatedBy) and a read of the last content review (B3). The restore action itself only needs UI over the existing rollbackPortalPublication (A1).
Working copy and a given snapshot rendered as a guest DTO, for the faithful draft/live/version preview and restore confirmation, plus a field-level diff in guest words (B4).
Try as guest: a preview-only resolver that writes no response, scan or notification and never navigates to Google (C9).

Review checklist assembled from existing reads (token, manager, Google destination, brand profile, wording per locale), each item labelled with who can fix it (A2), plus a contrast gate on the primary colour at publish (C2).
Property-level read of affected portals for property-wide edits, from portal_pending_content_changes (B5), plus batch review and publish across portals, which is a decision.
Composition choice (A, B, C) on the brand profile, the derived-colour-role engine, the Folio night edition per portal, and a neutral hospitality default palette (C2).
Localized EN/BG link labels and category titles, and a curated iconKey set rendered in the admin and on the guest page (C3). Link approval state shown in place (A3).
Place type and placement naming, and several named access artifacts per portal (C4). Print-kit PDF generation per composition with the QR/NFC rules built in (C4).
Re-downloading a code without rotating it: encrypted token retrieval for Account admins and responsible managers, with an audit event. This is a security decision (C4).
Duplicate a portal / start from a copy (C5), and a suggested welcome line per place type.
Republish to adopt a new guest wording pack, with the language-pack version exposed per snapshot (C6).

Qualified scans for bounded windows, 'Guests who opened Google' and useful-link selections as separate measures filtered by portal_destination_kind (B6), plus the label fixes: retire 'Review Clicks' and the ambiguous 'Scans' (A9).
Property- and group-scope portal analytics: widen the portal.rating registry scope (a governance decision) or wrap queryGoalMetric (B7). Group analytics view.
Align the range model with the dashboard's ?range= (A8). Put the portal scans tile and the attention chip on Dashboard › Overview, and portal columns in the fleet (A4).
Inbox Feedback portal facet and a deep link from analytics to 'this portal's private notes' (B9).
List of guest responses under review, so the existing moderation function has a surface (B10).
Token and access-artifact history for the ledger (B11), and ledger events for kit downloads.
An 'Ask an Account admin' request notification (workflow_collaboration), and a needs_admin state for the setup step portal_published (C8).
Better portal.health_attention template: reason, fix and a deep link to ?tab=activity (today it is generic and opens Settings).
Excluding authenticated admin test scans from qualified_scans (a decision).
Permission alignment: delete link or category at portal.update, and archive portal allowed for Property managers in the UI (map D1). Both are product decisions.
concepts.risks:
**1. Preview drift destroys trust.** The whole concept rests on 'what you see is what guests get'. The admin preview must use the public renderer and resolver rules exactly, not a lookalike.
- Mitigation: one render path.
- Mitigation: visual regression that pins preview against /p for every state, composition and language.
- Mitigation: an admin-only 'hidden from guests' line, so filtering is visible rather than surprising.

**2. Hard dependency on publish-while-live.** Without the new command, 'Publish changes' would have to disable and republish, which causes the outage it promises to remove. Do not ship the workspace before the command exists.

**3. Measure mismatch.** Bounded-window 'Scans' today is operational `portal.scan`. Labelling it 'Qualified scans' would be dishonest. All admin figures need the bounded-window qualified read, and the fleet's scanCount must not be relabelled.

**4. A sortable portfolio can still be read as a ranking.**
- Mitigations: default attention-then-name sort, no rank numbers, medals or best/worst tint, and no cross-property 'top' copy.
- Accept: a user can still sort by average. That is an ordinary table affordance, not a leaderboard.

**5. Placement naming can leak staff attribution** ('Maria's tables'). Free text cannot be fully policed.
- Mitigations: a fixed place type, the helper 'Name a place, not a person', admin-only labels, and no per-person analytics dimension ever.

**6. Property-wide changes surprise managers who are editing.** Their preview changes under them. Mitigations: a toast in open workspaces, a ledger line, a pending-change fact, and the Live toggle to compare.

**7. Batch publish can feel like silent mass change.** Mitigation: per-portal diffs and checks with opt-out checkboxes. Otherwise fall back to one review per portal, which is a decision.

**8. Account-admin bottleneck in the beta.** Few Account admins own the look, the fallback wording, destinations and the Google connection. Mitigations: the needs_admin setup state, 'Ask an Account admin' requests naming the item, and the Waiting-for-you queue.

**9. Shown-once versus reprint.** Without a re-download decision, managers will rotate codes just to reprint, which breaks existing prints. Escalate the security decision early.

**10. Health can lie.** It may still say 'Working' after every code is revoked, if the reconciliation gap is real. Destinations that lapse vanish silently today. Verify both before health is marketed as monitoring.

**11. The workspace switch from standard page to icon rail may disorient occasional users.** It is consistent with the Inbox. Verify with 3 to 5 property managers on a moderated task: 'change the spa welcome line and republish', 'reprint the reception card'.

**12. Performance.** Composition fonts (about 95KB for Carved Stillness) inside an iframe, preview refreshes and a batched list projection must stay inside the app-page budget. Mitigations: debounce, keep the iframe alive across tabs, and cache the per-property font subsets.

**13. Scope creep.** Scheduling, per-link analytics, QR-versus-NFC splits and digests are deliberately deferred. The workspace must read as finished without them.

concepts.name: Portal Desk: running portals like inbox cases
concepts.thesis:
An operator's real job is not designing pages. It is keeping 10 to 200 live guest pages healthy across properties and changing one now and then. So portal administration becomes the inbox again, and each portal is a case.

- The rail answers two questions. "Where" is the property (or All properties), then a portal group. "What state" is one of the queues: Needs attention, Unpublished changes, Mine, Live, Drafts, Paused, Archived.
- The list uses fixed 78px rows that show exceptions first.
- The detail pane reads like an inbox case:
  - A facts toolbar: Live · version 4, Draft · 3 changes, codes, owners, group.
  - Attention lines, each naming one fix and who can do it.
  - A 30-day strip of vital figures.
  - A ledger of publications, restores, health changes, code events and brand events.
  - A draft dock at the bottom, the twin of the composer dock. It holds the pane's one primary action, Review & publish.

Three things happen outside the case. Editing is a mode you enter and leave: a focused studio (the owner's Refined Sections, made flatter) beside a device preview that shows exactly what guests see. Reading performance happens in one honest report written in the dashboard's grammar. Brand has its own Account Admin studio. Its changes wait in each live portal's draft, and the affected portals are listed.

Two guarantees hold throughout. Only a deliberate publish changes what guests see. Nothing in the admin can make Google depend on the score.
concepts.navigation:
Sidebar
- The Portals row (globe) is active in both scopes. In org scope it now opens /portals instead of being inert, the same way Reviews opens /inbox.
- Portals gets no nav badge. A red count for "Google link is being re-checked" would be alarmist. Attention reaches people through the bell, the Overview chip and the rail count.

Workspace geometry (the inbox's own numbers)
- 48px icon rail | queue rail 224 | list 400 (min 320, max 50%) | 6px resize handle | case (min 480, about 762 at 1440).
- Every column header is 56px.
- The desktop floor is 1078px. Below it, the queue strip plus the case sheet take over, exactly as in the inbox.

Queue rail, top to bottom
1. Scope select. Outline sm button, full width, `building-2`, searchable (the #582 pattern). It holds All properties plus each property. It is the only scope control; switching keeps the queue and the view.
2. Rail label PORTALS (the app's one uppercase style):
   - All portals `layers` (default)
   - Needs attention `triangle-alert` (count in #a45f00 beside the word)
   - Unpublished changes `file-pen`
   - Mine `circle-user-round` (portals I am a responsible manager of)
   - separator
   - Live `globe` · Drafts `circle-dashed` · Paused `circle-pause`
   - separator
   - Archived `archive`
   Zero counts print nothing.
3. Rail label GROUPS, at property scope only:
   - one 32px row per group with a member count;
   - a `triangle-alert` 12 glyph plus sr-only "1 needs attention" when a member does;
   - Ungrouped;
   - ghost "+ New group";
   - each row's ⋯ holds Rename and Archive group (Archive is Account Admin only).
   Selecting a group narrows the scope, and the list header's scope line reads "Avela Resort › Spa ×".
4. Footer (border-top):
   - Performance `chart-column` (hidden without `dashboard.use`);
   - Property brand `palette` (property scope only);
   - Keyboard shortcuts with Kbd "?".

URL contract (all state lives in the URL, as ADR 0057 does for queues)
- /properties/$id/portals?queue=attention|changes|mine|live|drafts|paused|archived&group=&portal=&q=&sort=attention|name|published|scans&filters…
- /portals?queue=…&propertyId=… (the propertyId deep link stays valid)
- /properties/$id/portals/$portalId/edit?section=welcome|links|note|languages|look|wording|internal&locale=en|bg&state=arrival|rating|after|after-1v5|note|done|google-unavailable|inactive-code|paused&width=390|320&compare=live
- /properties/$id/portals/new?step=placement|experience|review|share
- /properties/$id/portals/$portalId/publish (single review) and /properties/$id/portals/publish?portals=…&reason=brand|pack (batch)
- /properties/$id/portals/brand
- …/performance?range=30d|90d|180d|all&group=&portal= (the same ?range= as the Dashboard)

Legacy deep links map forward:
- ?tab=settings → edit
- ?tab=links → edit?section=links
- ?tab=share → the case with the codes sheet open
- ?tab=analytics → performance?portal=

Health notifications deep-link to the case, not to a tab.

Keyboard (legend on ? and in the rail footer)
- j / k: next / previous case
- Enter: open
- e: edit in studio
- p: preview
- x: select row
- /: search
- Esc: close the case, or leave the studio
- ?: legend
Leaving the studio returns to the same case, with the list scroll and selection kept.

screens.name: 1. Portals workspace, property scope (All portals)
screens.purpose: The daily home for one property's portals: see what is wrong and what is unpublished, then open a case. It replaces today's paged table, its swatch and badge columns, and the separate Portal groups section.
screens.layout:
1440×1024, mode B.
- Icon rail 48.
- Queue rail 224: scope select "Avela Resort ⌄"; PORTALS: All portals 7, Needs attention 1, Unpublished changes 2, Mine 3, ─, Live 5, Drafts 1, Paused 1, ─, Archived 2; GROUPS: Spa 2 (with the attention glyph), Restaurants 3, Ungrouped 2, + New group; footer: Performance, Property brand, Keyboard shortcuts ?.

  - Header 56: h1 "All portals" 14/600 with count 7 in 12px muted; scope line "Avela Resort"; then a ghost search icon, a ButtonGroup [Filters][Sort: Needs attention], and a primary sm "New portal" (the list area's one primary).
  - Rows are a fixed 78px, border-b, hover #f1f0fc, active #e7e4ff.
  - Gutter 20px: an 8px status dot (#101115 live, a hollow #b5b7bd ring for a draft, #b5b7bd for paused), replaced by `triangle-alert` 12 #a45f00 when the portal needs attention.

  - Lines 2–3 (clamped at 36px, muted): signals first at weight 500 ("Google link unavailable ·" in #a45f00; "3 changes not live ·" in #101115), then quiet facts: "Live · v4 · EN, BG · 412 scans · 4.6 from 180 · 30 days".
  - Trailing 44px column: the age of the last event ("2h") above the responsible manager's 20px disc.
- Case pane: see screen 2.
screens.keyInteractions:
- j / k walks the cases.
- Default sort is Needs attention, then name, so problems rise without a separate home.
- The checkbox appears on row hover or focus. With two or more rows selected, the list header becomes the bulk bar: "2 selected · Review & publish 2 · Choose manager · Move to group · Pause…".
- Filters popover: Reason, Owner, Language, Code state.
- An empty queue shows one sentence and one action, for example "Nothing needs attention. 5 portals are live." with a ghost "Show all portals".
- A property with no portals shows the dashed EmptyState "No portals yet" / "A portal is the page guests reach from a QR code or NFC card at one place, like reception or a table." with "New portal".
- With exactly one portal, its case opens on arrival.
